inventory.granularity: One identifiable player behavior or grouped runtime service. Related routines, script variants, stages, files and content records are evidence components, not additional feature counts.
inventory.core_function_scope: Listed functions cover each behavior core. Supporting features are dependencies. Virtual calls, SDK/hardware routines and asset-driven closure remain to audit.
inventory.interpretation: C recovery is not new gameplay implementation. The baseline matching executable retained original functions in C plus assembly. Runtime acceptance is separate.
inventory.baseline_feature_count_note: The before count retrospectively applies this same inventory to the saved pre-prompt function statuses. It is not a claim that an exhaustive feature inventory existed before this prompt.

native_ai.scope: Original native scripted behavior, perception and timing; distinct from modern AI/LLM additions.

examples.observation: Triggered effect clears flashback list; otherwise issues a movement command.
Tick/state sequence branches on action, updates aim/fall poses, effects and notifications.
Facing/proximity gates timed control lock, motion/camera and later restoration.

native_ai.limitations: Callbacks include NPCs and moving props; this is not a unique-character count, exhaustive AI feature count or runtime acceptance.

tooling_scope.user_confirmed: Recover original NPC behavior and add separately measured AI-assisted tools, analysis and modding.

bounded_execution_evidence.scope: Bounded models and explicit external contracts; separate from whole-callback acceptance.

unresolved_scope.description: No supplied developer-authored exhaustive feature list; 40 groups are provisional, not an official total.
Disc assets, command records, cinematics and placements need semantic inventory/runtime coverage; retained bytes are not content acceptance.
Unknown vtable slots, types and callback edges leave call-graph closure incomplete.
Exact menu labels, rare state/RNG/card/reset/error behavior still needs observation.

A pinned PS1 emulator comparison environment is available and recorded video/state/PCM subsets match. Exhaustive SDK/hardware timing, video/audio events, memory-card errors and disc behavior still require coverage and independent review.
User confirmed original NPC behavior and separate AI-assisted analysis/modding tools. Tooling additions do not change canonical gameplay or count as original features.
